title: Neck vessel ultrasound
what: The doctor uses a probe to look at the arteries in your neck that carry blood to the brain. The scan shows plaques, narrowing, and how blood flows.
why: For dizziness, noise in the head, after a stroke or mini-stroke, high cholesterol or blood pressure, or before heart surgery.
tell_doctor: If you have had a stroke or surgery on your neck vessels

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable that leaves your neck bare. Take off necklaces and earrings before the scan.

prepare.title: Before you go in
prepare.text: You are usually advised not to smoke or drink strong coffee for a couple of hours before. Check with your clinic.

bring: A towel or tissues, if your clinic asks
steps: You lie on your back, and your head is turned slightly to one side
Cool gel is put on your neck
The doctor moves the probe along one side of your neck, then the other
Sometimes you hear a whooshing sound. This is the sound of blood flow
The gel is wiped off, and you get up
feel: Cool gel and light pressure from the probe
after: You usually get the report right away
You can go back to your day right away
Your doctor will tell you what to do next
red_flags: Sudden weakness or numbness in an arm, leg, or one side of the face, trouble speaking, or a drooping face may be a stroke. Call emergency services right away

faq.a: They are the large blood vessels in the neck that carry blood to the brain.

faq.q: Do I need to prepare for a neck vessel ultrasound?
faq.a: No. You can eat and drink. Just keep your neck bare, with no jewelry.
